core_obligations: Start from the duality identities (proof lines 13194-13199): for a left dual (N, eta, epsilon) use the composition identities to control maps into and out of M, which is the tool used throughout.

Reduce to a local problem (proof lines 13200-13207): by the local nature of the properties involved, it suffices to find a covering of each object U such that the restrictions of M are represented by strictly perfect complexes, so one may work with concrete complexes.

Develop the truncation argument (proof lines 13210-13256): for a chosen complex M^bullet representing M, use the duality identities together with truncations to produce, for each degree range, a subcomplex through which the identity of M factors; this is the technical core and is used repeatedly afterwards.

Get boundedness and boundedness above (proof lines 13259-13275): applying the argument to the dumb truncation sigma_{>= a} tau_{<= b}M^bullet shows first that M lies in D^b(O) and then allows choosing M^bullet bounded above with terms that are direct sums of a controlled kind.

Reach pseudo-coherence and then perfection (proof lines 13278-13413): assuming M has tor amplitude in [a, b], the same argument shows that M is m-pseudo-coherent, and the successive improvements of the representative show that on the members of a covering M is represented by a strictly perfect complex; the dual computed from that representative is then identified with the abstract left dual N through the identities from the first paragraph.
proof_roadmap: Use the unit and counit of the duality to obtain the two composition identities.
Since perfection is local, work with an explicit complex representing M and use the identities to build subcomplexes through which the identity factors.
Apply the construction to truncations to get boundedness, boundedness above and pseudo-coherence of M.
Improve the representative on a covering until it is strictly perfect, and identify the dual so obtained with the given left dual.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that having a left dual in D(O) forces an object to be perfect and forces the dual to be the canonical one (statement lines 13185-13192). The proof is a long technical development with a clear architecture: the duality identities are converted into factorisation statements for the identity through suitable subcomplexes of any chosen representative (proof lines 13210-13256); applying these to dumb truncations yields boundedness and then a bounded above representative of a controlled shape (proof lines 13259-13275); the same machinery, under the extra hypothesis of tor amplitude, gives m-pseudo-coherence and finally a strictly perfect representative on the members of a covering (proof lines 13278-13413); the dual computed from that representative is then identified with the abstract left dual using the identities of the first paragraph. The claim is H2: the argument is long and technically demanding but is written out in full and depends only on the duality identities and standard local constructions.
